# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**My top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299).** Runner's World names them best overall. They have a clear sound, physical buttons that are easy to use mid-run, and a clip design that stays put. They're only IPX4 and last about 7 hours, so skip them if you run in heavy rain. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Best for maximum awareness: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list.** This is a bone-conduction neckband that Runner's World and SoundGuys both pick in that category. It has IP55 protection, about 12 hours of battery, and physical controls. Sound is bassier but less clear than the Bose, and the band can get in the way of long hair or winter hats. Runner's World lists it at $125 at Walmart and $130 at Lowe's, so compare prices. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/))
- **Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200.** They last 10 hours (40 with the case) and are rated IP57, and WIRED named them best overall. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80.** It has an IP55 rating, 10-hour battery, and a 10 g hook design. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon, and Dealectric's page covers it too. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [Dealectric, affiliate link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2))
- **Cheapest way to try the style: JLab Flex Open, about $40.** Sound is thinner, but Runner's World calls it a low-risk starter. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))

**Also worth a look:** SoundGuys picks the Nothing Ear (Open), about $99, as the best open-ear pick overall and the best for running. It has an IP54 rating and strong bass for the category. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))

**Price check:** Dealectric lists the AeroFit 2 at $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20. SoundGuys shows it at $79.99 on Amazon, so that "deal" looks worse than the regular price. Check current prices before buying.

**Caveats:** Open-ear designs don't block sound, so they're quieter in traffic and leak audio to people nearby. Keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings. I don't have direct product-page links for the Bose or Shokz models. The articles linked above list the retailers, including Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and the brands' own stores.

If you tell me your budget and whether you wear glasses, hats, or have long hair, I can narrow this to one pick.
